literal: Xin did not want this and also did not know the matter; he then said to his son-in-law Pei You: "Li Fu and I, though our clans are far apart, are close as one family.
idiomatic: Xin did not want it and claimed ignorance; he told his son-in-law Pei You, "Li Fu and I are distant kin but close as kin.

literal: In office there was this urging; yesterday I drew a hairpin and stabbed myself, took a belt and strangled myself, yet could not die.
idiomatic: They pressed me in office; yesterday I stabbed myself with a hairpin and strangled with a belt and still could not die.

literal: And I also do not know the affair."
idiomatic: And I do not even know the affair."

literal: You said: "Why die for another?"
idiomatic: You said, "Why die for someone else?"

literal: The Fu brothers' guilt is plain.
idiomatic: The Fu brothers' guilt is obvious.

literal: There is one Feng Lan whom Fu had killed earlier; that family hates him bitterly.
idiomatic: Feng Lan was killed by Fu before; his family hates Fu bitterly.

literal: Just call Lan's younger brother and ask — enough to know the whole.
idiomatic: Call Lan's younger brother and ask—that is enough to know everything.

literal: Xin followed his advice.
idiomatic: Xin did as he said.

literal: Also Fan Biao of Zhao commandery fully listed the Fu brothers' conduct; the authorities reported upward, and Fu was convicted.
idiomatic: Fan Biao of Zhao also laid out the Fu brothers' deeds; the authorities reported up and Fu was convicted.

literal: An edict listed Xin's greed as deserving death, but because he had exposed the Fu brothers he was spared.
idiomatic: An edict said Xin's greed deserved death, but because he had exposed the Fu brothers he was spared.

literal: One hundred lashes, tonsure, and assignment as menial.
idiomatic: He received a hundred lashes, was shaved, and made a menial.

literal: When Xin was disgraced, Marquis of Pingshou Zhang Dan saw Xin and spoke with him, finding him remarkable.
idiomatic: When Xin fell, Marquis of Pingshou Zhang Dan met him and found him remarkable.

literal: He told others: "This is a fine man; he will not long remain bent."
idiomatic: He said, "This is a fine man; he will not stay bent long."

literal: Before long he was again Grand Director of the Granary, acting southern-section affairs.
idiomatic: Soon he was again Grand Director of the Granary, acting for the southern section.

literal: Using Fan Biao's submitted plan, he ordered that beyond a thousand li each household separately transport grain to the granary.
idiomatic: He used Fan Biao's plan: beyond a thousand li each household had to transport grain to the granary.

literal: This made localities pile up grain, stalled for months.
idiomatic: Local stores piled up and stalled for months.

literal: The people competed with bribes to get ahead in line; near and far were greatly exhausted.
idiomatic: People bribed to go first; near and far were ruined.

literal: The roads resounded with talk: "A hoarding minister is worse than a thieving minister."
idiomatic: On the roads people said, "A hoarding minister is worse than a thief minister."

literal: Xin's younger brother Left Army General Pu said to Xin: "Fan Biao is good at winning men with a pleasant face and lending them fine words; one never hears talk of virtue and duty, only of power and profit.
idiomatic: Xin's brother Pu, Left Army General, said, "Fan Biao wins men with a pleasant face and fine words; you never hear virtue, only profit.

literal: His words taste sweet; watch his deeds and they are thievish — the so-called flatterer, slanderer, greedy traitor.
idiomatic: His words are sweet; his deeds are theft—flatterer, slanderer, greedy traitor.

literal: If you do not cut him off early, regret will not reach you."
idiomatic: Cut him off now or regret it later."

literal: Xin would not listen, trusted him all the more, and told Biao everything in his heart.
idiomatic: Xin would not listen; he trusted Biao more and told him every secret.

literal: Xin was favored by Xianwen, took part in deciding great military and state counsels, also held selection of officials — power tilted inside and outside; the hundred offices all bent the knee to serve him.
idiomatic: Favored by Xianwen, Xin joined in army and state counsels and held selection; power leaned inside and out; every office bowed to him.

literal: Biao for no merit was enfeoffed and made magistrate of Lu'nu.
idiomatic: Biao, without merit, was made magistrate of Lu'nu.

literal: When Xianwen died, Xin was moved to Minister of Works, advanced to Duke of Fanyang, out as Palace Attendant, Regional Commander of the South, General Who Opens Offices with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies, Governor of Xuzhou.
idiomatic: When Xianwen died Xin became Minister of Works, Duke of Fanyang, Palace Attendant, Regional Commander of the South, General Opening Offices with Three Excellencies' rank, Governor of Xuzhou.

literal: Fan Biao knew Empress Dowager Wenming's anger at Xin and knew inside and outside resented him; in Taihe year 1 he reported to her will that Xin was plotting outside rebellion.
idiomatic: Biao knew Empress Dowager Wenming hated Xin and that court and country resented him; in Taihe 1 he reported Xin was plotting rebellion outside.

literal: The empress dowager summoned Xin to the capital and stated his rebellion.
idiomatic: The empress dowager summoned Xin to the capital and charged rebellion.

literal: Xin said: "There is none."
idiomatic: Xin said, "There is none."

literal: Biao was brought to testify against Xin.
idiomatic: Biao was called to testify against Xin.

literal: Xin said: "You falsely claim to know me — what more can I say!"
idiomatic: Xin said, "You lie that you know me—what can I say!"

literal: "Yet you disregard the deep kindness I showed you and could bear this — inhuman in the extreme."
idiomatic: Yet you forget my deep kindness and do this—inhuman in the extreme."

literal: Biao said: "Your grace to Biao — how does it compare with Li Fu's grace to you?"
idiomatic: Biao said, "Your grace to me—how does it compare with Fu's grace to you?"

literal: "You once could bear to harm Fu; how dare Biao not bear to harm you now?"
idiomatic: You once harmed Fu; how dare I not harm you now?"

literal: Xin sighed: "I did not heed Pu's words and brought this grief on myself — ten thousand regrets in the heart; too late to sigh!"
idiomatic: Xin sighed, "I ignored Pu and brought this on myself—regret beyond words, too late to sigh!"

literal: He was then executed.
idiomatic: He was executed.

literal: Pu, styled Jizhi, nature thick and honest, knew many men.
idiomatic: Pu, styled Jizhi, was thick and honest and knew many men.

literal: Enfeoffed Marquis of Yiyang, Grand Minister of Sacrifices.
idiomatic: Enfeoffed Marquis of Yiyang, Grand Minister of Sacrifices.

literal: Han Yanzhi, styled Xianzong, native of Duyang in Nanyang, descendant of Wei Minister of Works Han Ji.
idiomatic: Han Yanzhi, styled Xianzong, of Duyang in Nanyang, descended from Wei Minister of Works Han Ji.

literal: Served Jin, post of General Who Establishes Might, staff officer of Jingzhou, transferred to chief clerk of the Pacify-the-West headquarters.
idiomatic: He served Jin as General Who Establishes Might, Jingzhou staff officer, then chief clerk of the Pacify-the-West headquarters.

literal: When Jin general Liu Yu attacked Sima Xiuzhi, before reaching Jiangling he secretly wrote Yanzhi a letter to win him.
idiomatic: When Liu Yu attacked Sima Xiuzhi, before reaching Jiangling he secretly wrote to win Yanzhi.

literal: Yanzhi replied; the words were very fierce: "Liu Yu beneath your feet: who in the realm does not see your heart, yet you would again deceive the state's gentlemen!"
idiomatic: Yanzhi's reply was fierce: "Liu Yu, every man under heaven sees your heart—yet you would deceive the state's gentlemen again!"

literal: His unbending was thus.
idiomatic: He was that unbending.

literal: The affair is in the Basic Annals of Song in the History of the Southern Dynasties.
idiomatic: The affair is in Song's Basic Annals in the History of the Southern Dynasties.

literal: Because Yu's father's name was Qiao, styled Xianzong, Yanzhi therefore styled himself Xianzong and named his son Qiao — showing he would not serve the Liu house.
idiomatic: Yu's father's name was Qiao, styled Xianzong; Yanzhi styled himself Xianzong and named his son Qiao—refusing to serve the Liu.

literal: Later he fled to Yao Xing.
idiomatic: Later he fled to Yao Xing.

literal: In Taichang year 2 he entered Wei with Sima Wensi and others.
idiomatic: In Taichang 2 he entered Wei with Sima Wensi and others.

literal: Emperor Mingyuan made Yanzhi Regional Commander of Wulao, enfeoffed Marquis of Luyang.
idiomatic: Mingyuan made him Regional Commander of Wulao, Marquis of Luyang.

literal: Earlier Yanzhi had come and gone at Bai'gu Walled Town, visited the tomb of Lu Zongzhi, and had a mind to end his days there.
idiomatic: Earlier he had visited Lu Zongzhi's tomb at Bai'gu Walled Town and wished to end his days there.

literal: He therefore told Zongzhi's grandson: "The Luo and Yi rivers were capitals for three dynasties; the court will surely dwell here.
idiomatic: He told Zongzhi's grandson, "Luo and Yi were capitals for three dynasties; the court will surely live here.

literal: When I die, do not trouble to bury me in Northern Dai; you may bury me right here."
idiomatic: When I die do not bury me in Northern Dai—bury me here."

literal: The son followed his words and buried him beside Zongzhi's tomb.
idiomatic: His son obeyed and buried him by Zongzhi's tomb.

literal: More than fifty years later Emperor Xiaowen moved the capital; several of Yanzhi's households lived north of the ancestral tomb at Bai'gu Walled Town.
idiomatic: Fifty years later Xiaowen moved the capital; Yanzhi's kin lived north of the tomb at Bai'gu.

literal: Yuan Shi, styled Jizu, native of Yangxia in Chen commandery, descendant of Han Minister of Works Yuan Pang.
idiomatic: Yuan Shi, styled Jizu, of Yangxia in Chen, descended from Han Minister of Works Yuan Pang.

literal: Father Shen, Jin Palace Attendant.
idiomatic: His father Shen was Jin Palace Attendant.

literal: Shi in the south held the post of Consulting Staff Officer to Prince of Wuling Wang Zun.
idiomatic: In the south Shi was consulting staff officer to Prince of Wuling Wang Zun.

literal: When Liu Yu seized power, Shi went to Yao Xing.
idiomatic: When Liu Yu seized power Shi went to Yao Xing.

literal: When Yao Hong was destroyed he came to Wei as a honored guest, enfeoffed Viscount of Yangxia.
idiomatic: When Yao Hong fell he came to Wei as honored guest, Viscount of Yangxia.

literal: With Minister of Works Cui Hao one meeting made them sworn friends as men of the state.
idiomatic: One meeting with Cui Hao made them sworn friends as men of the state.

literal: At the time court ritual and statutes all came from Hao; Hao because Shi was broad in old precedents, whenever he drafted something always consulted him.
idiomatic: Court ritual then came from Hao; Hao, because Shi knew old precedent, always consulted him when drafting.

literal: By nature a man of long years; though drifting in exile he kept pure poverty and measure, not losing a gentleman's integrity.
idiomatic: He was a man of long years; though exiled he stayed poor and measured, never losing a gentleman's line.

literal: Men of the time greatly respected him; all called him Consultant Yuan.
idiomatic: His time respected him; all called him Consultant Yuan.

literal: In Yanhe year 2, Defender-General Prince of Le'an Fan was Governor of Yongzhou; edict had Shi and Vice Director of Secretariat Gao Yun both as consulting staff officers.
idiomatic: In Yanhe 2 Prince of Le'an Fan, Defender-General, was Governor of Yong; Shi and Secretariat Vice Director Gao Yun were made his consulting officers.

literal: He declined and was excused.
idiomatic: He declined and was excused.

literal: Shi was serene and loved the Way, broadly read records and transmissions, especially fond of glossing the Cangjie and Erya.
idiomatic: Shi was serene, loved the Way, read widely, especially glossing Cangjie and Erya.

literal: He composed "Explanation of Characters" but did not finish.
idiomatic: He wrote "Explanation of Characters" but did not finish.

literal: In the second year of Yitai'an he died, posthumously Governor of Yuzhou, posthumous name Marquis Su.
idiomatic: In Yitai'an 2 he died, posthumously Governor of Yuzhou, posthumous name Marquis Su.

literal: Son Ji inherited the father's title, post of Administrator of Wei commandery, government with a pure reputation.
idiomatic: Son Ji inherited, was Administrator of Wei commandery, famed for pure rule.

literal: Added title General Who Pacifies the Distance.
idiomatic: He was given supernumerary rank General Who Pacifies the Distance.

literal: When Prince of Song Liu Chang opened his headquarters, Ji was summoned as consulting staff officer.
idiomatic: When Prince of Song Liu Chang opened headquarters Ji was summoned as consulting officer.

literal: Mao Xiuzhi, styled Jingwen, native of Yangwu in Xingyang.
idiomatic: Mao Xiuzhi, styled Jingwen, of Yangwu in Xingyang.

literal: For generations the house served Jin.
idiomatic: His house served Jin for generations.

literal: When Liu Yu pacified Guanzhong he left his son Yizhen to garrison Chang'an, making Xiuzhi marshal.
idiomatic: When Liu Yu pacified Guanzhong he left son Yizhen at Chang'an with Xiuzhi as marshal.

literal: When Yizhen was defeated Xiuzhi was taken at Tongwan.
idiomatic: When Yizhen fell Xiuzhi was taken at Tongwan.

literal: When Taiwu pacified Helian Chang he obtained him.
idiomatic: Taiwu pacified Helian Chang and took him.

literal: He was made to lead Wu troops; for merit enfeoffed General of Wu Troops.
idiomatic: He was set to lead Wu troops and enfeoffed General of Wu Troops for merit.

literal: Xiuzhi could make southern food and personally season it, often to satisfaction.
idiomatic: Xiuzhi could cook southern food and season it himself to please.

literal: Taiwu personally favored him, repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of Masters of Writing, enfeoffed Duke of Nan commandery, constantly in the Imperial Kitchen directing imperial meals.
idiomatic: Taiwu favored him, raised him to Vice Director, Duke of Nan, always in the Imperial Kitchen directing meals.

literal: On campaign against Helong, when the armies besieged the city the traveling palace had few men; Song's old general Zhu Xiuzhi was General of Yunzhong and wished to lead Wu troops in revolt.
idiomatic: Besieging Helong the camp had few men; Song's Zhu Xiuzhi, General of Yunzhong, wished to lead Wu troops in revolt.

literal: He entered Helong hoping to float south by sea and return.
idiomatic: He entered Helong hoping to sail south by sea.

literal: He told Xiuzhi; Xiuzhi would not listen and he stopped.
idiomatic: He told Xiuzhi; Xiuzhi refused and he stopped.

literal: That day without Xiuzhi a great upheaval nearly happened.
idiomatic: That day without Xiuzhi a great disaster nearly came.

literal: Zhu Xiuzhi then fled to Feng Hong.
idiomatic: Zhu Xiuzhi fled to Feng Hong.

literal: Xiuzhi again for military merit was promoted Special Advancement, General Who Pacifies the Army, rank below Cui Hao.
idiomatic: Xiuzhi rose again for merit to Special Advancement, General Who Pacifies the Army, below Cui Hao.

literal: Hao because he was an old house of China, though not broadly versed still dipped into books and records, and debated with him.
idiomatic: Hao, because he was an old Chinese house, though not broad still read books and debated with him.

literal: Next they reached Chen Shou's "Records of the Three Kingdoms"; he said "it has the air of an ancient good historian; what he wrote is canonical in meaning — since Ban Gu none match Shou."
idiomatic: They came to Chen Shou's "Records of the Three Kingdoms"; Hao said it had the air of a good ancient historian, canonical since Ban Gu.

literal: Xiuzhi said: "In Shu I once heard elders say Shou had been a clerk under Zhuge Liang and was flogged a hundred strokes, so in judging the Martial Lord he wrote: adapting to change was not his strength."
idiomatic: Xiuzhi said, "In Shu elders said Shou had been Zhuge Liang's clerk, was flogged a hundred times, so he wrote the Martial Lord was weak at adaptation."

literal: Hao then argued: "Chen Shou's judgment of Liang was praise beyond measure from old obligation, not words of resentment."
idiomatic: Hao argued, "Shou's judgment of Liang was old obligation praising too much, not resentment."

literal: Liang's serving Bei was the time when hero and lord met; ruler and minister matched, fish and water as metaphor.
idiomatic: Liang serving Bei was hero and lord meeting, ruler and minister like fish and water.

literal: Yet he could not contend with Cao for the realm, abandoned Jingzhou, retreated into Ba-Shu, held poor rugged ground, styled himself emperor among border barbarians — this is the lowest stratagem.
idiomatic: Yet he could not fight Cao for the realm, abandoned Jingzhou, retreated to Ba-Shu, held poor hills, styled himself emperor among barbarians—the lowest stratagem.

literal: He may be paired with Zhao Tuo, yet to rank with Guan Zhong and Xiao He — is that not excessive!
idiomatic: He may match Zhao Tuo; to rank with Guan Zhong and Xiao He—is that not too much!

literal: Moreover Liang held Shu, did not measure strength, used harsh law to control Shu men, wished with border barbarians' masses to resist the central state.
idiomatic: Moreover Liang held Shu, misread strength, ruled Shu with harsh law, wished border tribes to resist the center.

literal: He sent troops out Longyou, twice attacked Qishan, once attacked Chencang, slow and missing the moment, broken and returned.
idiomatic: He marched from Longyou, twice attacked Qishan, once Chencang, slow and late, broken and back.

literal: Later he entered Qin River valley and again sought field battle.
idiomatic: Later he entered Qinchuan and again sought battle in the open.

literal: The Wei men knew his intent and wore him down without fighting.
idiomatic: Wei knew his mind and wore him down without fighting.

literal: Wits exhausted, power spent, he fell ill and died.
idiomatic: Wits gone, power spent, he fell ill and died.

literal: By this speaking, how does he fit an ancient good general who sees difficulty and knows when to stop?
idiomatic: By that measure, how is he an ancient good general who sees difficulty and stops?

literal: Xiuzhi said Hao's words were right.
idiomatic: Xiuzhi said Hao was right.

literal: Later he died as Grand Director of the Outer Capital Kitchen, posthumous name Duke Gong.
idiomatic: Later he died as Grand Director of the Outer Capital Kitchen, posthumous Duke Gong.

literal: Xiuzhi in the south had four sons; only son Faren entered Wei.
idiomatic: In the south Xiuzhi had four sons; only Faren entered Wei.

literal: At the start of Wencheng he was Director of the Gold Bureau, inherited the title, transferred to Director Within the Hall.
idiomatic: At Wencheng's start he was Director of the Gold Bureau, inherited the title, then Director Within the Hall.
